The applied recon:disc score ratio (and FM-in-score flag) for a 'what carries the detector' / score-formula panel MUST be resolved in this order; do NOT read config.score_recon_disc_ratio alone — it is ABSENT/null on backfilled runs (the field was added to config.py:223 after the 271 baseline) and would render the panel blank.
order: experiment_metadata._lambda_recompute.ratio  (provenance string, e.g. '4:1'; present on recomputed/backfilled runs; read alongside _lambda_recompute.fm_in_score)

_meta.usage: Backend/frontend bind to `entries[metric_key]`. If a key is absent, run `fallback.rules` against the key name to synthesize an entry and set inferred=true. An unknown metric is ALWAYS still displayed (never dropped), badged 'inferred'.

field_contract.family: one of: detection.threshold_free | detection.point | detection.pak | detection.range | detection.ar | detection.teacher | diagnostic.separation | diagnostic.disturbing | diagnostic.grl | diagnostic.scad | diagnostic.array | loss.training | meta.timing | meta.count | meta.threshold | meta.config | uncategorized
field_contract.direction: up (higher-better) | down (lower-better) | neutral (context/diagnostic, do not rank)
field_contract.phase_validity: all (valid incl. pre-warmup) | post-warmup (mask while epoch <= teacher_only_warmup_epochs)
field_contract.unit: score [0,1] | loss | ratio | snr | count | seconds | threshold | label | quantile | mixed
field_contract.viz_hint: object: {chart, direction, group, mask_prewarmup?, annotate?, source?, split_by?, cache?, secondary?}

fallback.principle: NEVER drop an unknown metric. Display it, infer family+direction from name patterns below, set inferred=true and inferred_direction=true, badge it in the UI. Pre-warmup masking defaults ON for any inferred key whose name matches the post-warmup patterns.
fallback.rule_match_semantics: A rule fires if the key matches its `match_substring` (any listed substring is contained in the key) OR its `match_regex` (re.search). Rules are tried in `rule_order`; the FIRST firing rule wins; if none fire, `default_entry` is used. Both fields are optional per rule.

rules.note: P1-01: context/schedule/count keys are never ranked. The count anchors are ANCHORED (^n_anom / \bn_(...)\b / count$) — the old loose 'n_anom'/'n_norm'/'count' substrings COLLIDED with loss magnitudes (recoN_NORMal, recoN_ANOMaly, recon_anomaly_std, studeNT_..._NORMal, train_studeNT_recon_aNOMaly) and mis-resolved them to neutral; anchoring confines the match to genuine count keys (n_anomaly/n_normal/n_pure_normal/n_disturbing_normal). See resolver_self_test.

FB-R4-03 (verified run_base_experiments.py:843-855): epoch_{recon,disc}_ratio_{normal,anomaly,disturbing} is the per-sample-type CONTRIBUTION SHARE of that component in the adaptive score — disc_ratio = disc_contrib / (recon_contrib + disc_contrib) ∈[0,100]. It shows WHERE the score comes from, NOT detection/separation quality, so it is NEUTRAL/context — NOT an anomaly/normal (a/n) ratio. ANCHORED so it matches ONLY this per-type contribution-share family. Placed BEFORE snr_separation so it wins even if the key ever reaches the fallback path outside the history namespace. The TRUE best-epoch a/n ratios are the SEPARATE explicit entries loss_stats.recon_ratio / loss_stats.disc_ratio (direction up) and are untouched; *_SNR / cohens_d / *_separation still resolve up via snr_separation.

separation/effect-size: higher=better; sign matters (negative=anti-correlated, warn). NOTE (FB-R4-03): the recon_ratio/disc_ratio substrings here are for the TRUE best-epoch a/n ratios (loss_stats.recon_ratio/disc_ratio, which have explicit up entries anyway); the per-type CONTRIBUTION-SHARE family epoch_{recon,disc}_ratio_{type} is caught EARLIER by the anchored contribution_share rule (neutral) and never reaches this rule.

P1-06: anchored/suffix patterns only. The old bare 'recon'/'discrepancy' substrings were a latent mislabel trap (a future renamed 'recon_quality_score' would be force-labeled down/loss). recon_ratio/recon_SNR are caught earlier by snr_separation; explicit recon_*/disc_* magnitudes have explicit neutral entries (P1-02). NOTE: a bare 'recon*'/'discrepancy*' key with no _loss/_error suffix now falls through to the default (uncategorized/neutral, badged inferred) rather than being mislabeled a loss.

pak_auc_f1.description: K-integrated point-adjust F1 (K=0..100). THE primary selection/ranking metric (config.best_epoch_metric).

pak_auc_f1_raw.description: PA%K-AUC F1 at fixed (non-best) threshold. Secondary/diagnostic view.

pak_auc_f1_t_raw.description: PA%K-AUC time-series F1 at fixed threshold.

roc_auc.description: Area under ROC; rank quality, prevalence-insensitive (0.5=random). Optimistic on imbalanced TSAD.

prc_auc.description: Area under precision-recall (average precision). Honest threshold-free metric under imbalance.

vus_roc.description: Volume-Under-Surface ROC (range-tolerant). P1-04: per-epoch VUS density is RUN-DEPENDENT — dense on full runs (271/PSM: 100/100 non-null) but may be sparse/null on lite per-epoch runs (run_base_experiments.py:746-749 lite=True skips VUS). Verify non-null density before animating as a dense trend.

vus_pr.description: Volume-Under-Surface PR (range-tolerant). Best threshold-free range metric but expensive. P1-04: per-epoch density is run-dependent (dense on 271/PSM = 100/100; may be sparse on lite runs). Verify non-null density before animating.

f1_score.description: sklearn point-level F1 at F1-optimal threshold. NO point-adjustment — the honest point F1.

optimal_threshold.description: Score threshold chosen by F1-optimal search. Context, not quality.

f1_t.description: Time-series-aware F1 (range precision/recall) at the optimal threshold.

affiliation_f1.description: Affiliation interval F1 (rewards being near an event).

r_based_f1.description: Range-based F1 (Tatbul NeurIPS'18) overlap-based interval F1.

anomaly_ratio.description: Fraction of points labeled anomaly. Context for the _ar threshold.

f1_ar.description: Point F1 at the leakage-free (1-AR)-quantile threshold.

teacher_prc_auc.description: PR-AUC of teacher-reconstruction-only score. Valid all phases.

teacher_pa_20_f1.description: Point-adjust K=20 F1 of teacher-recon-only score.

teacher_pak_auc_f1.description: Teacher-only PA%K-AUC F1. Overlay vs pak_auc_f1 to see discrepancy contribution post-warmup.

teacher_pak_auc_f1_raw.description: Teacher-only PA%K-AUC F1 at fixed threshold.

recon_snr.description: Teacher-recon normal-vs-anomaly separation (mean_diff/(sigma_a+sigma_n)). Valid pre-warmup. >0.8 strong, <0.1 none; negative=anti-correlated (warn).

disc_snr.description: Student-teacher discrepancy separation. POST-WARMUP only (random student pre-warmup => masked, Option-C). Negative=anti-correlated.

disturbing_roc_auc.description: Separability of pure-normal vs disturbing-normal (hard negatives in anomaly windows).

n_disturbing_normal.description: Count of normal windows inside anomaly segments. Context.

fm_loss.description: Hidden-level teacher-student distance (training loss). DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — NOT part of the inference score since 2026-06-01.

grl_cls_loss.description: Adversarial classifier loss. Lower=classifier fits, but the system goal is reversed-gradient feature suppression — NOT a quality metric.

grl_balanced_acc.description: P1-05. In grl_mode=='classifier': balanced accuracy of the GRL classifier ([0,1]; high acc can mean features still leak anomaly identity, which GRL tries to reduce). In grl_mode=='wdgrl' (trainer.py:706-723): a Wasserstein-critic score proxy = abs(critic_norm - critic_anom) — UNBOUNDED, can exceed 1. Read config.grl_mode before labeling the axis. Diagnostic/context, never ranked.

grl_anomaly_acc.description: P1-05. classifier accuracy on anomaly patches ([0,1]) in grl_mode=='classifier'; raw mean Wasserstein-critic score on anomaly features (unbounded, can be negative) in grl_mode=='wdgrl'. Context (NOT higher-better) — read config.grl_mode.

grl_normal_acc.description: P1-05. classifier accuracy on normal patches ([0,1]) in grl_mode=='classifier'; raw mean Wasserstein-critic score on normal features (unbounded, can be negative) in grl_mode=='wdgrl'. Context — read config.grl_mode.

grl_acc_gap.description: |normal_acc - anomaly_acc|. Context. In wdgrl mode this is a difference of unbounded critic-score proxies (not in [0,1]).

discrepancy_loss.description: Output discrepancy training loss (normal+anomaly margin). 0 pre-warmup (gated).

train_rec_loss.description: Per-epoch joint reconstruction loss (legacy alias t_loss; NOT 'teacher loss').

train_disc_loss.description: Per-epoch output-discrepancy loss (== loss_stats.discrepancy_loss; legacy alias s_loss). 0 pre-warmup.

train_teacher_recon_normal.description: Teacher-only recon loss on normal samples (SKILL t_re). Valid pre-warmup.

train_teacher_recon_anomaly.description: Teacher-only recon loss on anomaly samples (context — higher than normal is expected/good for detection).

train_student_recon_normal.description: Student-only recon loss on normal samples (SKILL s_re). 0.0 sentinel pre-warmup (student frozen).

train_student_recon_anomaly.description: Student-only recon on anomaly samples. Context; masked pre-warmup.

_per_k_values.description: K=0..100 grid (x-axis for the PA%K curve).

_per_k_f1.description: F1 vs K curve underlying pak_auc_f1.

_infer_feature_disc_mean.description: Per-feature mean discrepancy at inference (len=num_features). Which sensors drive disagreement.

_train_feature_recon_mean.description: Per-feature mean recon error in training (len=num_features).

_train_feature_recon_max.description: Per-feature max recon error in training.

_train_feature_disc_mean.description: Per-feature mean disc in training. NULL during warmup — guard.

_train_feature_disc_max.description: Per-feature max disc in training. NULL during warmup — guard.

recon_normal.description: P1-02. Mean teacher-recon error on NORMAL samples (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context, NOT a lower-better loss: the rankable signal is the recon_ratio (anomaly/normal, up) and recon_SNR (up), NOT this raw magnitude. Pairs with recon_anomaly; recon_anomaly > recon_normal is GOOD for detection.

recon_anomaly.description: P1-02. Mean teacher-recon error on ANOMALY samples (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context: a HIGHER value than recon_normal is GOOD (anomalies reconstruct worse) — so a blanket lower-better-loss label is WRONG. Rank by recon_ratio/recon_SNR (up), not this magnitude.

recon_disturbing.description: P1-02. Mean teacher-recon error on DISTURBING-NORMAL samples (normal points inside anomaly windows; hardest negatives). NEUTRAL context; rank by recon_cohens_d_disturbing_vs_anomaly (up).

recon_pure_normal.description: P1-02. Mean teacher-recon error on PURE-NORMAL samples (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context; the separation ratios/SNR are the rankable signals.

disc_normal.description: P1-02. Mean output-discrepancy on NORMAL samples (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context; rank by disc_ratio/disc_SNR (up), not this magnitude. Post-warmup only (random student pre-warmup).

disc_anomaly.description: P1-02. Mean output-discrepancy on ANOMALY samples (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context: HIGHER than disc_normal is GOOD (teacher↔student disagree more on anomalies). Rank by disc_ratio/disc_SNR (up). Post-warmup only.

disc_disturbing.description: P1-02. Mean output-discrepancy on DISTURBING-NORMAL samples. NEUTRAL context; rank by disc_cohens_d_disturbing_vs_anomaly / disc_SNR_disturbing (up). Post-warmup only.

disc_pure_normal.description: P1-02. Mean output-discrepancy on PURE-NORMAL samples. NEUTRAL context; separation ratios/SNR are the rankable signals. Post-warmup only.

recon_normal_std.description: P1-02. Dispersion of recon_normal (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context, NOT a lower-better loss; feeds the SNR denominator.

recon_anomaly_std.description: P1-02. Dispersion of recon_anomaly (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context; feeds the SNR denominator.

disc_normal_std.description: P1-02. Dispersion of disc_normal (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context; feeds the SNR denominator. Post-warmup only.

disc_anomaly_std.description: P1-02. Dispersion of disc_anomaly (loss_stats). NEUTRAL context; feeds the SNR denominator. Post-warmup only.

loss_stats.recon_SNR.description: Teacher-recon separation (best-epoch loss_stats). Source for recon_snr.

loss_stats.recon_ratio.description: Mean recon anomaly/normal (>1 = anomalies score higher).

key_namespaces.note: Same metric name appears in multiple containers. Resolve by stripping the namespace prefix then looking up `entries`; the semantics are identical across containers.
key_namespaces.score_variants: experiment_metadata.json::{metrics|teacher_recon_metrics|student_recon_metrics|disc_metrics}.<key> — same metric family on a different score. `metrics`=adaptive(primary), teacher_recon=teacher-recon-only (==metrics pre-warmup), student_recon=student-recon-only, disc=raw discrepancy. All higher-better.
key_namespaces.loss_stats: experiment_metadata.json::loss_stats.<key> — best-epoch separation/loss diagnostics (25 keys; see loss_stats.* entries).
key_namespaces.anomaly_type: anomaly_type_metrics.json::<TYPE_NAME>.<metric> — per-anomaly-type breakdown; TYPE_NAME is DYNAMIC dataset vocabulary; per-type metrics reuse the same `entries` semantics (count/mean_score/std_score neutral; roc_auc/prc_auc/precision/recall/f1_score/detection_rate up).
key_namespaces.history: training_histories.json::['0'].train_* — per-step/epoch training curves; map to entries by name (lower-better losses, neutral schedules).

history_families.note: P4B-01 / RT-1 / P3-03 + FB-R4-03. The non-train_* per-training-epoch families have a DOCUMENTED family/direction so the F5 catalog groups them under diagnostic.context (or diagnostic.separation) instead of 'uncategorized'. The resolver applies these patterns (regex over the key) ONLY in the history namespace, AFTER explicit entries and BEFORE the generic fallback.rules; the FIRST matching pattern wins. FB-R4-03: the per-sample-type CONTRIBUTION-SHARE family epoch_{recon,disc}_ratio_{normal,anomaly,disturbing} = disc_contrib/(recon_contrib+disc_contrib) per type (run_base_experiments.py:843-855) is NEUTRAL/context (it shows WHERE the score comes from, not detection/separation quality), so it is matched FIRST by an ANCHORED context pattern — it is NOT an anomaly/normal (a/n) ratio. The TRUE a/n ratios are the SEPARATE best-epoch explicit entries loss_stats.recon_ratio/disc_ratio (up), untouched. The residual ^epoch_.*_ratio_ separation pattern (kept below) only catches OTHER per-epoch ratio series that are not this contribution-share family; the context magnitudes (recon_score/disc_score/raw_*) are rescued by the next pattern.

resolver_self_test.note: P1-01 + P1-06 verification suite. The backend's fallback resolver MUST pass these assertions (run over the 271/PSM key inventory + the named collision keys). Lookup precedence is: explicit `entries[strip_namespace(key)]` first; only if absent, run `fallback.rules` in `rule_order`. A key with an explicit entry is exempt from the fallback assertions (its explicit direction/family governs).

assert_no_loss_magnitude_in_explicit_neu.rule: When resolved via FALLBACK ONLY (ignoring explicit entries), none of these magnitude keys may land in the explicit_neutral rule (would mis-color as neutral/count and drop from rankings). Must instead hit snr_separation / lower_better_loss / default.

assert_count_keys_still_neutral.rule: Genuine count keys MUST still resolve to explicit_neutral via the anchored regex.

assert_bare_recon_not_forced_loss.rule: P1-06: a future bare 'recon*'/'discrepancy*' name with NO _loss/_error suffix must NOT be force-labeled down/loss by lower_better_loss; it falls through to default (uncategorized/neutral, inferred).

assert_separation_still_up.rule: Separation/ratio/SNR keys remain up (caught by snr_separation before lower_better_loss).
